audit.bitsandbytes_int8_path: NOT SUPPORTED by vLLM 0.28.0 (bitsandbytes is not a valid quantization method)
audit.int8_alternative: fp8 (native hardware INT8/FP8 via vLLM fp8 backend on RTX 4090)
audit.notes: vLLM 0.28.0 does NOT support bitsandbytes INT8 quantization. The HF checkpoint uses bitsandbytes INT8 which cannot be loaded directly in vLLM. Closest vLLM-supported 8-bit path is FP8 (via quantization='fp8'). FP8 is NOT the same as bitsandbytes INT8: it uses hardware FP8 GEMM, different precision semantics, and requires re-quantization of the model weights. No conversion of bitsandbytes INT8 → vLLM-native INT8 is available without retraining/re-quantization.

explicit_questions.Q1_did_vllm_improve_bf16_latency: YES — vLLM BF16 E2E 1043.8 ms vs HF BF16 1285.0 ms (-241.2 ms, 61.3 vs 50.4 tok/s)
explicit_questions.Q2_did_vllm_improve_int8_latency: N/A — bitsandbytes INT8 is not supported by vLLM 0.28.0. Direct INT8 comparison impossible. FP8 results shown instead.
explicit_questions.Q3_int8_memory_advantage_preserved: vLLM FP8 VRAM = 5.06 GB vs vLLM BF16 = 8.05 GB. FP8 saves 2.99 GB (37.1% reduction). Original HF bitsandbytes INT8 advantage (4.60 vs 8.02 GB, ~43%) not directly comparable.
explicit_questions.Q4_int8_slower_due_to_backend_overhead: HF bitsandbytes INT8 was 4.24× slower than HF BF16 (5450 vs 1285 ms E2E). vLLM FP8 (native hardware FP8 GEMM) is only 1.13× slower than vLLM BF16 (1182.5 vs 1043.8 ms). Hardware FP8 GEMM overcomes the software bitsandbytes dequantisation overhead.
explicit_questions.Q5_int8_suitable_for_concurrency_testing: NOT as bitsandbytes INT8 — incompatible with vLLM. vLLM FP8 is suitable for concurrency testing (stable latency, good throughput). Recommend converting to GPTQ/AWQ/FP8 checkpoint for a proper INT8-class vLLM benchmark.
